title: I shipped a production AI system solo. Here's the build log.
linkedinPost:
84% of developers use AI tools. Fewer than 1 in 10 ship to production.

Here is what the other 9 miss — from 6 solo AI builds shipped in 18 months.

"Production" is not a codebase milestone. It is an operational posture. A prototype fails silently. A production system alerts, degrades gracefully, and has a recovery path you can follow at 11pm without Slack.

My honest timeline across 6 builds:
• Content automation pipeline: 3 weeks spec to live
• Language exam app (850+ questions, GDPR Art. 17, Google Play): 8 weeks
• Average across all 6: 5–6 weeks for a full-stack, compliant, user-facing system

What I would actually do starting a solo AI build today:

• Write the spec before touching code. 20+ pages minimum. Every decision made under time pressure is worse than the one made in a document.
• Commit to the 3-Seam Stack: n8n for orchestration, Supabase for data, one primary LLM with a documented fallback. Build everything else as a replaceable seam.
• Set GDPR and EU AI Act compliance as a launch gate. August 2, 2026 changed what "we'll handle compliance later" means in practice.
• Instrument from day one. PostHog EU-hosted + Sentry with UUID-only identity. You cannot improve what you cannot measure.

Revenue per employee increases when you remove the handoff between intent and deployed system. Solo builds are the extreme version of that thesis — one person, full stack, production output.

Full piece + the exact stack and timeline across 6 builds — link in comments.

mainEntity.name: What is a solo production AI build?

acceptedAnswer.text: A solo production AI build is a full-stack, deployed, user-facing AI system built without a permanent engineering team. 'Production' means automated error handling, GDPR or relevant compliance by design, and infrastructure that runs without constant manual intervention — not a prototype or local demo.

mainEntity.name: What tools do solo AI builders use in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: The reliable production stack: n8n Cloud for orchestration, Claude API for language tasks, Supabase for database and auth, OpenAI Realtime for voice, ElevenLabs for TTS, RevenueCat for subscriptions, PostHog (EU-hosted) for analytics, Sentry for crash reporting. The key principle is clean integration seams — every tool should be replaceable without rebuilding the system.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to build a production AI system solo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Based on 6 builds completed between 2024 and 2026: 3–8 weeks for a full-stack, GDPR-compliant, user-facing system. Fastest was a content automation pipeline (3 weeks). Most complex was a language exam app with AI scoring and speaking practice (8 weeks). Average is 5–6 weeks.

mainEntity.name: What does the EU AI Act mean for solo AI builders shipping in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: From August 2, 2026, high-risk AI systems require documented risk management, transparency measures, and human oversight before EU deployment. For most solo builders in fintech tools, productivity software, or education, the immediate obligations are transparency documentation and, where applicable, conformity assessment. GDPR remains the higher-friction requirement for day-to-day operation.
